bib.title: Bandit Algorithms, Chapter 19: Stochastic Linear Bandits

question: How can UCB be generalised to stochastic bandits whose expected reward is linear in an unknown parameter, and what regret does it get?
hypothesis: Optimism over a confidence ellipsoid around the regularised least-squares estimate gives regret of order d*sqrt(n) up to logs.
contributions: Defines the stochastic contextual and stochastic linear bandit models
Defines LinUCB (UCB over a confidence set C_t) with a regularised least-squares estimator and ellipsoid confidence sets
Proves Theorem 19.2 (regret bound) via the elliptical potential lemma 19.4
Computation, notes and exercises (generalised linear bandits, spectral bandits, implementation)

results.claim: A valid confidence width is sqrt(beta_n) = sqrt(lambda) m2 + sqrt(2 log(1/delta) + d log((d lambda + n L^2)/(d lambda))), where m2 bounds ||theta*||_2 (proved as Theorem 20.5 in next chapter).

limits: Regret bound is worst-case, with little dependence on theta* or action-set geometry; instance-dependent bounds are open (Note 2).
Bound is vacuous when d is large or infinite (Note 1); effective dimension needed.
Regret definition is meaningful only when learner's actions do not greatly affect later contexts (Sec 19.1).
Computation of argmax over (a,theta) is bilinear; efficient only in special cases (Sec 19.3.1).
Cauchy-Schwarz step in Eq 19.11 often loses a logarithm (Note 4).
Noise fixed to 1-subgaussian; confidence-set construction deferred to Chapter 20.
Bound tight up to logs only for infinite or exponentially large action sets (Note 5; Chapter 24).
Generalised linear bandit bound depends unpleasantly on link function (Note 7).
practices: Use regularised least squares (lambda>0) so the estimator is unique even if actions do not span R^d (Eq 19.4, Sec 19.2).
With a small finite action set pick A_t = argmax <thetahat_{t-1}, a> + sqrt(beta_t) ||a||_{V_{t-1}^{-1}} by iterating over arms (Eq 19.13).
Prefer the data-dependent beta_t of Eq 19.14 over Eq 19.8 (Note 3).
Update V_t^{-1} with Sherman-Morrison for O(k d^2) per-round cost (Exercise 19.8d).
With a fixed large action set, run LinUCB in phases ending when log det V_t grows by log(1+eps) to cut compute (Exercise 19.4).
